scientific_purpose: Bound whether a 14.692km disagreement between two historic Ledda published labels resembles spatial separation between author-referenced colony site and actual georeferenced huddle observations in a different Antarctic cohort.

source_dynamic.public_literature: LaRue et al 2026 Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation doi:10.1002/rse2.70083
source_dynamic.phenology: SAR huddle centroids throughout Antarctic autumn and winter, date-specific

frozen_image_eligibility: areasum > 0, both geodetic huddle-centroid coordinates finite and inside WGS84 bounds, named colony in fixed roster; never use image area0 records as biological absent sites

geometry.distance: great-circle haversine Earth mean radius 6371.0088 km
geometry.site_label_rule: compare author-published static source site centroid to each SAR-derived huddle mean centroid without optimizing anchor

limitations: Source SAR colonies were deliberately monitored at known sites, so 0/54 beyond 3km would NOT prove all emperor movements stay inside 3km
Winter 2024 single-year huddle positions at six different colonies cannot prove Ledda moved or did not move ~14.7km in 2009-2014
Source author static positions are approximations and SAR tracking centroid is a detected group average, not a boundary of the full colony or every possible subgroup
The dynamic SAR source and the earlier 2024 model roster are related via LaRue authorship, not an entirely independent set of observers
Published 2026 high-resolution SAR study has already established these colonies' seasonal behaviour, phenology and movements; do not claim movement discovery
No wildlife movement causal mechanism, reproduction, true founding, neighbour rescue or novel island rule identified
analysis_claim_allowed: descriptive cross-dataset geospatial support comparator for 2024 winter at six selected colonies only
